Class SkullEyeGameTestsLogic

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.gametest.SkullEyeGameTestsLogic
public final class SkullEyeGameTestsLogic extends Object
Googly eyes on placed mob heads: applying and harvesting them through EyeItemService.useOnSkull(Player, Level, InteractionHand, BlockHitResult), an eyed mob's own head inheriting its eyes (EyeItemService.markHeadDrop(LivingEntity, ItemStack), reached through each loader's death-drop hook), breaking and re-placing a head, and saving one. The loader adapters' protection-mod ordering is exercised by native item-denial tests on Forge and NeoForge; the rendered eyes and their client-side expressions need a client.

For the in-game steps below, get Optometrist shears as described in EyeItemServiceGameTestsLogic.

  • Method Details

    • placedHeadUsesSharedAmbientSlots

      public static void placedHeadUsesSharedAmbientSlots(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      In game: give a placed head a one-eye layout and enable blink and cross-eye at the shortest interval. Walk away and return during a blink. The head resumes at the current blink phase and its unpaired pupil never crosses.

    • deniedItemUseLeavesHeadsUntouched

      public static void deniedItemUseLeavesHeadsUntouched(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, BiConsumer<net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult, Boolean> interact)
      A native item-use denial prevents both applying and harvesting head eyes, without consuming the item, damaging shears, or spawning a drop. No in-game form without a protection mod that denies item use while leaving the click event uncanceled; guards that such a denial leaves the head, the item, and the shears as they were.

    • slimyEyeGivesAPlacedHeadEyes

      public static void slimyEyeGivesAPlacedHeadEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      A Slimy Eye gives an eyeless placed head eyes carrying its appearance; an eyed head refuses another. In game: dye a Googly Eye purple, craft it into a Slimy Eye, place a skeleton skull, and right-click the skull with it in survival; the skull gains purple googly eyes, a squelch plays, and the Slimy Eye is used up. Right-click the same skull with a second Slimy Eye; nothing happens and it is kept.

    • slimyEyeRefusesUnconfiguredHeadsAndTheSwitch

      public static void slimyEyeRefusesUnconfiguredHeadsAndTheSwitch(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      A head without a definition, or any head while the switch is off, refuses a Slimy Eye. In game: right-click a placed dragon head with a Slimy Eye; nothing happens and the Slimy Eye is kept. Set googlyEyesEnabled = false and right-click a skeleton skull; nothing happens either.

    • optometristHarvestsAPlacedHead

      public static void optometristHarvestsAPlacedHead(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      Optometrist shears take a head's eyes off as one Googly Eye; plain shears leave them. In game: give a skeleton skull purple eyes with a Slimy Eye, right-click it with plain shears (nothing happens), then with Optometrist shears; the eyes vanish, a purple Googly Eye pops out, the shearing sound plays, and the shears lose one durability.

    • brokenHeadKeepsItsEyes

      public static void brokenHeadKeepsItsEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      Breaking an eyed head drops a head item carrying its eyes, and placing that item restores them. In game: give a skeleton skull purple eyes, break it in survival, and hover the dropped skull; its tooltip lists googly eyes and the iris color. Place it again; it shows the same purple eyes in the same arrangement. Remove the eyes and break it again; the plain dropped skull carries no eye component and stacks with ordinary skulls.

    • eyedMobDropsAnEyedHead

      public static void eyedMobDropsAnEyedHead(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      An eyed mob's head inherits the mob's eyes; an eyeless mob's head doesn't. In game: give a skeleton purple eyes with /sg admin eyes true and /sg admin tint iris 0.6 0.1 0.8, then let a charged creeper blow it up; its dropped skull lists googly eyes and the iris color, and placed it shows the skeleton's purple eyes. A plain skeleton killed the same way drops a plain skull.

      TODO: this test fails on both loaders for reasons not yet understood, though the behavior works in game; its loader wrappers are commented out until the cause is found.

    • headEyesSurviveSaveLoad

      public static void headEyesSurviveSaveLoad(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A head's eyes survive saving and loading its block entity. In game: give a placed skeleton skull purple eyes, leave and rejoin the world; the eyes are still there.

    • adventureCanPlaceOnReadsTheClickedHead

      public static void adventureCanPlaceOnReadsTheClickedHead(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      In Adventure mode an item's CanPlaceOn list is read against the head itself, from any side. In game: in Adventure mode, hold a Slimy Eye given with [can_place_on={blocks:"minecraft:skeleton_skull"}] and right-click a skeleton skull's side; it gains eyes. Hold one listing minecraft:stone and right-click the top of another skull standing on stone; nothing happens.

    • eyeUsesAreCountedInStatistics

      public static void eyeUsesAreCountedInStatistics(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Applying and harvesting count as using the item. In game: note the Used counts of Slimy Eye and Shears on the Statistics screen's Items tab, apply a Slimy Eye to a cow and to a skeleton skull, and take the skull's eyes with Optometrist shears; Slimy Eye rises by two and Shears by one.

    • headKeepsOnlyItsEyeState

      public static void headKeepsOnlyItsEyeState(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A head keeps only its eye state from the data it loads, so nothing else a head item carried is saved or sent to players. In game, in creative: /give a skeleton skull whose block_entity_data has a somegoogly:data compound with hasGooglyEyes true and an extra key, and place it; /data get block shows the eye state without that key.

    • spectatorsLeaveHeadsAndThemselvesAlone

      public static void spectatorsLeaveHeadsAndThemselvesAlone(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Spectators cannot use eye items on heads or shear themselves. In game: in spectator mode, hold a Slimy Eye and right-click a skeleton skull, then sneak and right-click with shears while wearing eyes; nothing changes and nothing is used up.
